sitePin: Always use this language on this site
noteSameLanguage: This text already seems to be in your target language ({language}).
firstRunText: Translations are made into {language}. Is that the language you want?
optTtsFallback: Use the browser voice when a word has no recording
optTtsFallbackHelp: In this browser the built-in voice ends every word with a loud click, so Wordvault plays recordings from Wikimedia Commons instead. Turn this on to hear the built-in voice, click included, for words that have no recording.
tbEmptyHint: Double-click a word on any page, then press “Add to vault”.
dtNoDictionary: Wiktionary has no entry for this word.
dtDictionaryError: Could not load dictionary data. It will be tried again next time.
dtYourSentence: from the page you saved it on
bkHelp: Download your vault as a JSON file, or add the words from a file exported on another device. Importing never overwrites words you already have.
bkImported: {added, plural, one {Added # word.} other {Added # words.}} {duplicates} were already in your vault, {failed} could not be read.
bkBadFile: This file is not a Wordvault backup.
syncIntro: Keep the vault the same on all your devices. Nothing leaves this browser until you choose one of the ways below and confirm it.
syncModeOffHelp: Nothing is connected. Exporting above is your backup.
syncModeBrowserHelp: Uses your browser's own sync. Small: about 100 KB, for lists of up to a few thousand words.
syncModeCloudHelp: Google Drive, OneDrive or Dropbox: one file in the app's own folder in your account.
syncModeServerHelp: WebDAV (Nextcloud, ownCloud …) or a simple HTTP endpoint you run yourself.
syncOffExplain: The vault stays in this browser only. To have it on another device as well, choose one of the ways above.
syncBrowserWhere: In your browser's sync storage, which travels with your browser account (Firefox Sync, Chrome sync) like bookmarks do.
syncGdriveWhere: In the hidden app data folder of your Google Drive. It does not show among your files; you can see and delete it in Drive under Settings → Manage apps → Wordvault.
syncOnedriveWhere: In your OneDrive, in the folder Apps → Wordvault, as the file wordvault-vault.json.gz.
syncDropboxWhere: In your Dropbox, in the folder Apps → Wordvault, as the file wordvault-vault.json.gz.
syncWebdavWhere: On your server, as the file wordvault-vault.json.gz in the folder you named:
syncHttpWhere: On your server, behind the address you entered:
syncWebdavHelp: The address of a folder on your WebDAV server, your user name there and an app password (in Nextcloud: Settings → Security → Devices & sessions). The folder is created if it is missing.
syncHttpHelp: The address of a server that speaks Wordvault's small protocol (GET and PUT at /vault; see docs/self-hosted.md, which comes with a ready-made example server) and the key it expects.
syncBrowserExplain: Your browser carries the vault to your other devices signed in to the same browser account, compressed. There is room for about 100 KB; how full it is will be shown here. When it is full, synchronisation stops and the vault stays whole on this device.
syncSetupMissingText: Developer setup is missing for this provider: no client ID has been entered yet. Follow the steps in SETUP-OAUTH.md (in the repository), put the ID into src/sync/config.js and build again.
syncNotAvailable: This way of synchronising is not part of this version.
syncConfirmWhat: Your saved words will be sent to {service}: each word with its translation, its language pair, a short context sentence and your review progress. Page addresses, settings, API keys and sign-in data are never sent.
syncConfirmMerge: If a Wordvault file is already there, it is merged with this vault. No word is lost on either side.
syncConfirmReplace: The connection to {service} that is in use now is dropped. What it has stored stays where it is.
syncUsageWarning: Almost full. When it is full, synchronisation stops and the vault stays on this device. A cloud account or your own server has room for more.
syncDisconnectNote: The vault on this device stays as it is. It is no longer kept in step with your other devices.
syncDeleteRemoteHelp: Your other devices keep their own copies, but can no longer exchange them through it.
syncDisconnected: Disconnected. What was stored there has been left in place.
syncDisconnectedDeleted: Disconnected, and the stored file was deleted.
syncErrAuth: access was withdrawn or has expired; connect again
syncErrServerAuth: the server did not accept the user name, password or key
syncErrQuota: there is no room left there; the vault stays whole on this device
syncErrConflict: another device kept writing at the same time
syncErrIncomplete: the stored copy is still arriving
syncErrBadDocument: what is stored there is not a Wordvault file; it was left untouched
syncErrNewerSchema: what is stored there was written by a newer version of Wordvault; update this one
syncErrPermission: the browser did not give access to that address
syncErrInsecure: the address has to start with https:// (http:// is only accepted for localhost)
syncErrUrl: this is not a usable address
syncErrPassword: the password is needed, or the one given does not open the stored file
syncEncStateOn: on: only readable with your password
syncEncOff: The stored file is not encrypted: whoever runs the place it is kept in could read it. You can encrypt it with a password that never leaves this browser.
syncEncOn: The stored file is encrypted with your password before it leaves this browser. Nobody can read it without the password.
syncEncOffNote: If you turn it off, turn it off on all your devices: a device that still has it on will encrypt the file again.
syncEncWarning: If you lose this password, nobody can recover the stored copy. The vault on this device is not encrypted and is not affected. Your other devices will ask for the same password.
syncEncRememberHelp: Otherwise the password is asked for again each time the browser has been closed. Only a key made from the password is kept, never the password itself.
syncEncNeeded: The stored file is encrypted. Enter its password to synchronise on this device.
syncEncMismatch: The two passwords are not the same.
syncIcloudNote: iCloud is not offered: a browser extension has no way of reaching iCloud Drive. Export the vault as JSON above and save the file into your iCloud Drive folder instead.
quizWrong: Not this one. The right answer is marked.
quizUnknownHint: Counts as a wrong answer; the right one is shown
quizLaterHint: Doesn't count; the word comes back in a few minutes
quizNotificationText: Click to answer a question about one of your words.
optQuizHelp: From time to time Wordvault asks you about saved words: in the popup of its toolbar button, in a small window, or as a card on the page. Every word in the vault gets its turn; the ones you get wrong come back sooner.
optQuizEnabledHelp: While this is off no quiz appears and the timer does not run.
optQuizIntervalHelp: A quiz comes this often while you browse. A change counts from the moment you make it.
optQuizQuestionsHelp: With more than one, the next question follows in the same place and a short summary comes at the end.
optQuizDisplayHelp: If the way you choose is not possible at that moment, the next one is used. The panel below says which one it was and why.
optQuizNotify: System notification as a last resort
optQuizNotifyHelp: Only when none of the ways above can show a quiz, Wordvault tells you with a notification; clicking it opens the quiz. This needs the browser's notification permission.
optQuizNotifyDenied: the browser did not grant the permission
optQuizNotifySent: sent; click it to open the quiz
optQuizAllowNotDue: Also ask words that are not due yet
optQuizAllowNotDueHelp: When no word is due for review, the hardest one is asked anyway. Off: no quiz until a word is due.
optQuizMinCardsHelp: The quiz starts once the vault holds this many words.
optQuizTimeoutHelp: A card nobody answers closes after this long and does not count.
quizVerdictYes: Nothing stands in the way. Next quiz: {time}
quizDiagAskableValue: {words} words with a translation into {language}; {meanings} different meanings (at least {needed} needed)
quizOutcomeTimeout: not answered in time, skipped (does not count)
quizWhyBelowMinCards: the vault holds {total, plural, one {# word} other {# words}}, the quiz starts at {min}
quizWhyNotEnoughChoices: only {meanings} different meanings in {language}; four are needed for the choices
quizWhyWindowNotFocused: the browser window was not in front
quizWhyFullscreen: the page was in full screen
quizWhyAlreadyShowing: a quiz was already on screen
quizWhyPageNotSupported: extensions cannot show anything on the page that was open (a browser page, a new tab, or a tab opened before the extension was loaded)
quizWhyNothingDue: no word is due for review yet
quizDiagDisplay: Ways of showing it, in order
quizWhyMuted: switched off until tomorrow with “Not today”
quizWhyNoDisplay: none of the ways of showing it worked
quizWhyPopupUnsupported: this browser cannot open the toolbar popup by itself
quizWhyPopupRefused: the browser refused to open it
quizWhyWindowUnsupported: this browser cannot open windows for extensions
quizWhyWindowRefused: the browser refused to open it
quizWhyNotificationRefused: the browser did not show it
quizTestHelp: Shows a quiz right now the way the timer would, skipping the timer and every condition above. The line below says how it was shown.
quizTestFailed: The background script did not answer. Reload the extension.
optTargetLangHelp: Translations are made into this language. You can also change it from the translation popup.
optTargetLangUnset: Not chosen yet. Using your browser's language: {language}
optUiLangHelp: The language of Wordvault's own menus, buttons and messages. It does not change the language your words are translated into.
optDoubleClickHelp: Double-clicking a word on a page opens the translation popup.
errNetwork: Could not reach the translation service. Check your internet connection.
errTimeout: The translation service took too long to respond.
errRateLimit: The translation service's free limit has been reached. Try again later.
errUnsupportedLanguage: The translation service does not support this language pair. Try picking the languages above.
errTooLong: The selected text is too long to translate.
errContextInvalidated: Wordvault was updated. Reload this page to keep using it.
supportText: Wordvault is free, has no ads and collects nothing. If it helps you learn, a coffee keeps it going. Thank you!
welcomeLead: Learn words while you browse. Here is what you can do.
welcomeTranslateText: Double-click any word on a page: its translation opens right there, and you can listen to it.
welcomeVaultText: "Add to vault" saves the word with the sentence it came from. The toolbar button opens your vault.
welcomeQuizText: Now and then Wordvault asks you one of your words. The ones you miss come back sooner.
welcomeCaptionsText: On YouTube, rest the pointer on a word of the captions to translate it.
welcomeScanText: Text inside a video or a picture: pause, start the scan from the right-click menu, drag an area and click a word.
welcomeSyncText: Everything is kept in this browser. Synchronising with your own account or server is optional and off by default.
optOcrShortcutWarnOption: On a Mac, shortcuts with the Option key are unreliable (Option types special characters). Give this command a different combination, for example Command+Shift+E.
optOcrShortcutWarnNone: No shortcut is assigned (another extension or the browser may be using it). Assign one as described below, or start the scan from the right-click menu or the Wordvault button.
optOcrHelp: Reads the text in what is on screen, including text inside videos and pictures: pause the video, start the scan, drag an area. Click a word to translate it. The picture is read on this device, is not stored and never leaves the browser.
optOcrShortcutHelpChrome: If it is not assigned or does nothing, another shortcut is in its way: open the address below in a new tab and give "Scan text on screen" a key combination. Without a shortcut the scan can be started from the right-click menu of a page, or from the Wordvault button in the toolbar.
optOcrShortcutHelpFirefox: To change it: open about:addons (address below), click the gear button, then "Manage Extension Shortcuts". Without a shortcut the scan can be started from the right-click menu of a page, or from the Wordvault button in the toolbar.
optOcrShortcutAddress: Address of the browser's shortcut settings
optOcrLangHelp: Automatic reads with English and Turkish together. Choosing one is a little faster and a little more accurate for text in that language.
optOcrConfidenceHelp: Words the engine is less sure of than this (0 to 95) are left out. Lower it if words are missing, raise it if icons and shapes turn up as words.
optOcrShowBoxesHelp: For troubleshooting: draws a frame around every word that was found. When off, a word is only highlighted while the pointer is on it.
optOcrRememberHelp: The next scan starts with the area you scanned last; adjust it or press Enter.
optOcrEngine: Engine: Tesseract.js 7.0.0, running on this device. Language data included: English, Turkish.
ocrHint: Drag to choose an area · Enter or double-click: whole screen · Esc: cancel
ocrErrForbidden: This page cannot be scanned. Start the scan with the shortcut or the menu; browser pages and add-on stores do not allow it at all.
ocrErrRate: Too many scans in a row. Wait a second and try again.
ocrErrCapture: The screenshot could not be taken. Start the scan again with the shortcut or the menu.
ocrErrNoText: No text was found in this area.
ocrErrBlank: This content may not allow screenshots: the picture came back black (protected video does that).
ocrErrEngine: The text could not be read. Try again; if it keeps happening, reload the extension.
ocrResult: {count, plural, one {# word found} other {# words found}}
noteDamaged: {provider} sent this translation with some letters missing ("?" where a letter should be). Check it before you save it.
tbDamaged: {count, plural, one {# saved translation seems to have lost letters} other {# saved translations seem to have lost letters}} ("?" where a letter should be). Nothing was changed.
fbHelp: Found a bug or have an idea? Write it here. You see exactly what would be sent before anything is sent.
fbMessagePlaceholder: What happened, and what did you expect? For a bug: the steps that lead to it.
fbEmailHelp: Only if you want an answer. Leave it empty and the message is anonymous.
fbTechHelp: Browser and version, operating system, extension version, interface language, which features are on, kind of synchronisation. No pages, no words, no keys.
fbErrorsHelpCount: {count, plural, one {# record kept on this device} other {# records kept on this device}}: error message, part of the extension, time. No page addresses or content.
fbErrorsHelpNone: No errors have been recorded on this device.
fbShowData: Show the data to be sent
fbNothingSentYet: Nothing is sent by this button. You confirm on the next screen.
fbPreviewTitle: This is everything that will be sent
fbPreviewHelp: Exactly this, and nothing else. Go back to change it.
fbDestination: It goes to {host}, which passes it on to the developer and does not store it.
fbNotConfigured: Sending is not set up in this build yet (no feedback address). Nothing can be sent.
fbProblemLong: The message can be at most {max} characters.
fbProblemEmail: That does not look like an e-mail address. Correct it or leave it empty.
fbErrNetwork: Could not be sent: the receiver was not reached. Your text is kept; try again.
fbErrServer: Could not be sent: the receiver had a problem. Your text is kept; try again later.
fbErrRejected: The receiver did not accept the message ({reason}). Your text is kept.
fbErrRate: Too many messages in a short time. Your text is kept; try again later.
fbErrCooldown: Please wait {seconds} more seconds before sending again.
fbErrPermission: Not sent: permission to reach the receiver was not given.
errAuth: {provider} did not accept the API key. Check it in the settings.
errQuota: The character quota of your {provider} key is used up for this period.
errNoKey: {provider} is chosen but no API key is entered. Add one in the settings.
errProviderPermission: {provider} may not be reached yet. Open the settings and press "Test key" to allow it.
noteProviderFailed: {provider} is the service chosen in the settings. Nothing was switched; you can carry on with {fallback} for this lookup.
optProviderHelp: Used for everything Wordvault translates: words on pages, video captions and scanned text. Dictionary entries and example sentences come from Wiktionary whichever you choose.
optProviderMymemoryHelp: Free, no key needed. Limited to about 5,000 characters a day.
optProviderDeeplHelp: Needs your own DeepL API key. Fewer languages; the selected text goes to DeepL.
optProviderLanguage: {provider} does not translate into {language}, your target language. Translations will fail until you change one of the two.
optDeeplKeyHelp: Kept only in this browser. It is not part of the backup, of synchronisation or of feedback.
optDeeplOkUsage: The key works ({plan}). Used this period: {used} / {limit} characters.
optDeeplBadKey: DeepL did not accept this key. Check that it is copied whole, including ":fx" at the end if it has one.
optDeeplQuota: The key is valid, but its character quota for this period is used up.
optDeeplBusy: DeepL is receiving too many requests right now. Try again in a moment.
optDeeplNetwork: DeepL could not be reached. Check your internet connection.
optDeeplDenied: Not tested: permission to reach DeepL was not given.
optDeeplGuide1: Create a DeepL API account on DeepL's website (this is separate from the DeepL translator account).
optDeeplGuide2: Choose the free plan, "DeepL API Free".
optDeeplGuide3: Copy the key from the "API Keys" tab of your account and paste it above.
optDeeplGuideCard: DeepL may ask for a credit card when you sign up, to verify your identity, also for the free plan. The plan's limits and availability in your country are DeepL's; check them on its site.
optCacheHelp: Translations you looked up are remembered so that the same word is not asked for again. They are kept in three places:
optCacheLayerPage: In the page: a few answers, gone when the page is closed or reloaded.
optCacheLayerSession: For the session: shared by all tabs, gone when the browser is closed.
optCacheLayerWeek: On this device: kept through restarts; an answer nobody asked for in 7 days is deleted.
optCacheVault: The cache is not your vault. Saved words are never deleted automatically, and clearing the cache does not touch them. The cache is not part of the backup or of synchronisation.
optCacheFacts: Kept on this device now: {count, plural, one {# translation} other {# translations}} ({size}).
optCacheNoSession: This browser has no session storage; that part is skipped.
optCacheCleared: Cleared. Your vault was not touched.
quizWriteWrong: Not quite. The marked letters were wrong or missing.
quizHintHint: Shows one more letter. The answer then counts as partly right.
quizSkipHint: Shows the answer and counts as not known.
quizListenPrompt: Listen. What does it mean in {language}?
quizListenPromptSpelling: Listen. Which word did you hear?
quizNoVoice: This device cannot say this word aloud ({language}). Moving on to another word.
optQuizModesHelp: Only words in your vault are asked. Switch on as many ways as you like; with several on, each question draws one of them.
optQuizModeClassicHelp: The word is shown; pick its meaning from four.
optQuizModeWritingHelp: The meaning is shown; type the word.
optQuizModeListeningHelp: The word is said aloud and not shown; pick from four. Words your device cannot say are skipped.
optQuizAccentTolerantHelp: "cafe" counts for "café". Off: an accent that is missing or wrong is a spelling mistake.
optQuizListenAutoplay: Listening: say the word when the question appears
optQuizListenAutoplayHelp: Some pages do not let sound start by itself; the speaker button always works.
optQuizListenChoicesHelp: Meanings test understanding; spellings test hearing.
tbLearnedTotal: {count, plural, one {# word learned} other {# words learned}}
tbLearnedEmptyHint: A word is learned after several right answers in a row on different days. It stays in your vault and is asked only rarely.
freezeOffer: You missed yesterday. This week's freeze can keep your {count}-day streak.
rankRemaining: {count, plural, one {# more word to {rank}} other {# more words to {rank}}}
quizMuteWarning: If you skip today, your {count}-day streak resets.
reminderStreak: {count, plural, one {You have not done a quiz today yet. A few questions keep your streak going.} other {You have not done a quiz today yet. A few questions keep your #-day streak going.}}
reminderNoStreak: You have not done a quiz today yet. A few questions are enough to start a streak.
quizWhyQuietHours: it is within your quiet hours
optQuizLearnedStreak: Right answers in a row to learn a word
optQuizLearnedStreakHelp: They also have to fall on at least three different days. A learned word stays in your vault and is asked about once a month; a wrong answer makes it a word to learn again.
optQuizLearnedOtherHelp: At least one of those right answers has to be from a level above easy (typed or heard). Switch this off if you only use the classic way, or no word will ever count as learned.
optQuizDailyGoalHelp: A day counts for your streak once you answered this many questions on it, right or wrong.
optQuizFreezeHelp: Once a week a missed day can be covered, so a day without the browser does not end your streak. It is offered, never used by itself.
optQuizReminderHelp: One notification a day, only if the day's quiz is not done yet. Needs the notification permission above.
optQuizQuietHelp: No quiz and no reminder between these times. Leave both empty for none.
optQuizResetDone: The quiz settings are back to their defaults. Your words, streak and rank were not touched.
diffHardMode: Listening: hear it, pick from four
diffExpertMode: Listening + writing: hear it, type it
quizStartNoWords: There is no word with a translation in your vault to ask yet.
quizStartFewWords: This level needs at least {needed} different meanings to choose from; your vault has {have}. Save a few more words, or pick a level where you type.
quizStartNoFit: No word in your vault fits this level right now ({mode}).
quizStartNoVoice: This device cannot say your words aloud right now. Try a level without listening.
quizStartFailed: The quiz could not be started.
optQuizModeExpertHelp: The word is said aloud and nothing is shown; type what you hear.
optQuizModeNone: At least one way has to stay switched on.
optQuizModesManual: These are for the quiz that appears by itself. A quiz you start from the toolbar popup uses the difficulty chosen there, whatever is switched on here.
passagePartial: Only part of the text could be translated ({done} of {total} parts). {reason}
errPassageTooLong: The selection is too long: at most {max} characters are translated at once (selected: {selected}).
vaultAddPhraseHint: Kept as a phrase, apart from the word cards. The quiz does not ask phrases unless you switch that on in the settings.
selNothingSelected: Wordvault: select some text on the page first, then use the shortcut.
selNotHere: Wordvault: the shortcut does not work on this page. Select the text and use “Translate with Wordvault” in the right-click menu.
optSelHelp: Select a sentence or a paragraph on a page and translate it in one of three ways: the right-click menu, the small button next to the selection, or the keyboard shortcut. Up to {max} characters at a time; longer text goes to the translation service in parts that end where sentences end. A single selected word is looked up as a word, as before.
optSelMenuHelp: “Translate with Wordvault” in the menu of selected text. On pages where Wordvault cannot draw (the browser's own pages, its PDF viewer) the translation opens in a small window.
optSelButtonHelp: A small button next to a selection of more than one word. It does not appear for a single word or in text you are typing.
optSelShortcutHelpChrome: Translates the selected text. To change it, or if it is not assigned: open the address below in a new tab and give “Translate the selected text” a key combination.
optSelShortcutHelpFirefox: Translates the selected text. To change it: open about:addons (below), click the gear button, then “Manage Extension Shortcuts”.
optSelShortcutWarnNone: No shortcut is assigned (another extension or the browser may be using it). Assign one as described below, or use the right-click menu or the button next to the selection.
optSelShortcutWarnOption: On a Mac, shortcuts with the Option key are unreliable (Option types special characters). Give this command another combination, for example Command+Shift+U.
optSelPhrasesHelp: A translated selection can be kept in the vault as a phrase. Phrases are a kind of their own: the quiz asks only words unless this is switched on.
optSelPrivacy: The selected text is sent only to the translation service chosen above, and nowhere else. Nothing is kept unless you add it to the vault yourself. Note that MyMemory's free use is limited per day; long passages use it up quickly.
aiNeedsKey: To use this, enter your own AI key in the settings.
aiCopyPromptHint: Without a key: the ready prompt is copied and the site opens in a new tab; paste it there yourself. The answer does not come back to Wordvault.
aiConsentWord: The word, the sentence it is in and the page's title will be sent to {provider} and nowhere else. Its own terms apply to what it does with them. You are asked this once.
aiConsentPassage: The selected text and the page's title will be sent to {provider} and nowhere else. Its own terms apply to what it does with them. You are asked this once.
aiBy: Written by {provider} ({model}). AI can be wrong.
aiAddToNoteHint: Keeps this explanation with the word in your vault.
aiNotFromFields: Text selected inside a field you type in is not sent to an AI.
aiSiteSensitive: AI features are off on this site: it looks like a banking, e-mail or health site. You can allow it in the settings.
aiSiteBlocked: AI features are off on this site: it is on your block list.
aiErrAuth: {provider} did not accept the key: it is wrong, revoked, or may not use this model.
aiErrQuota: {provider}: the quota or the credit is used up, or too many requests were made. Try again later.
aiErrModel: {provider} has no model of that name (or the address is wrong). Check the model name in the settings.
aiErrOverloaded: {provider} is having trouble right now. Try again in a little while.
aiErrOrigin: Ollama turned the browser extension away. Start it with OLLAMA_ORIGINS set as described in the settings.
aiErrPermission: The browser has not been allowed to reach {provider} yet. Open the settings and press “Test”.
aiErrRefused: {provider} gave no answer for this text (its content rules).
aiErrEmpty: {provider} answered without any text. Try again.
aiErrAddress: The address is not usable: it has to start with https://, or with http://localhost for a server on this computer.
aiErrNetwork: {provider} could not be reached. Check the connection; for a server on this computer, check that it is running.
optAiHelp: Off by default. Connect an AI provider of your own and the translation popup gets “Explain with AI”. Nothing is sent by itself: every request is one you start by hand, and it goes straight from your browser to the provider you chose. Wordvault has no server in between. Translating, the vault and the quiz work without any of this.
optAiOffHelp: No AI provider. “Explain with AI” then only offers to copy a ready prompt for you to paste into a chat site yourself.
optAiGeminiHelp: With an API key from Google AI Studio. Has a free tier.
optAiClaudeHelp: With your own Claude API key from the Claude Console. Paid by use.
optAiOpenaiHelp: OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, LM Studio and others: you give the address, the key and the model.
optAiOllamaHelp: A model running on this computer. Nothing leaves it.
optAiKeyHelp: Stored only in this browser. It is not part of the backup, of synchronisation or of feedback, and it is sent only to this provider.
optAiKeyOptional: Leave empty if the server wants none (a server on this computer usually does not). Stored only in this browser.
optAiBaseHelp: The base address of the API. It has to start with https://, or with http://localhost for a server on this computer.
optAiModelHelp: The model's name exactly as the service writes it.
optAiModelHelpDefault: Leave empty for {model}, or type another model's name exactly as the provider writes it.
optAiModelExampleOllama: a model you have pulled, e.g. gemma4
optAiOk: It works: {provider} answered with the model {model}.
optAiDenied: The browser was not allowed to reach this address, so nothing can be sent. Press “Test” again and allow it.
optAiGeminiStep1: Open Google AI Studio (the link below) and sign in with a Google account.
optAiGeminiStep2: Create an API key there and copy it.
optAiGeminiFree: Free tier: Google's pricing page lists a free tier for several models, among them the default one here. It does not give fixed numbers; your limits per minute and per day are shown in AI Studio and can change. When a limit is reached the request fails until it resets.
optAiGeminiData: Data: the same page says that on the free tier content is “used to improve our products”, and on the paid tier it is not. Do not send text you would not want used that way.
optAiClaudeStep1: Open the Claude Console (the link below) and sign in.
optAiClaudeStep2: Create an API key under “API keys” and copy it.
optAiClaudePaid: The Claude API is billed by use and needs credit on the account; a Claude chat subscription is something else and does not include it.
optAiOpenaiStep1: Get the API's base address and a key from the service you use (for OpenAI the address is already filled in; OpenRouter: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1; LM Studio on this computer: http://localhost:1234/v1).
optAiOpenaiStep2: Type the model's name exactly as that service lists it.
optAiOpenaiStep3: Press “Test”; the browser asks once whether Wordvault may reach that address.
optAiOpenaiNote: What a service costs and what it does with the text you send is in its own terms.
optAiOllamaStep1: Install Ollama and pull a model (for example: ollama pull gemma4).
optAiOllamaStep2: Let it accept requests from browser extensions (see the note above), then restart it.
optAiOllamaStep3: Type the model's name above and press “Test”.
optAiOllamaLocal: The model runs on your computer: the text goes to localhost and no further. The first answer can take a while, because the model has to load.
optAiOllamaOrigins: Ollama only accepts requests from origins it knows, and a browser extension is not one of them by default. Start it with this variable (from Ollama's FAQ):
optAiOllamaMac: If Ollama runs as the macOS app: run {command} in Terminal, then quit and reopen Ollama.
optAiPrivacy: What is sent when you press “Explain with AI”: the word (or the text you selected), the sentence it is in and the page's title. Never: text from password fields, forms or boxes you type in, the page's address, or your vault. The first time, the popup tells you this and asks you to agree.
optAiConsentNone: You have not agreed to sending text yet; you will be asked at the first use.
optAiConsentGiven: You agreed to text being sent to {provider}.
optAiCache: Keep answers until the browser closes
optAiCacheHelp: The same question is then not sent (and paid for) twice. Answers are kept in memory only, never on disk, and are gone when the browser closes.
optAiBlocked: Sites where AI features are off
optAiBlockedHelp: One host per line (example.com covers its subdomains). Sites that look like banking, e-mail or health sites are off already.
optAiAllowed: Sites where they are on anyway
optAiAllowedHelp: For a site the built-in rule switches off by mistake. One host per line. Your block list above still wins.
optAiPromptSiteHelp: Which chat site is opened when no provider is connected. The prompt is on your clipboard; nothing is sent by Wordvault.
sumNoText: Wordvault found no main text to summarise on this page.
sumNotHere: Wordvault cannot read this page (browser pages, the PDF viewer and the add-on stores are closed to extensions).
sumParts: Sent in {parts} parts: {requests} requests (one per part, one to join them)
sumTruncated: The page is very long: only the first {limit} of its {total} characters will be summarised.
sumWasTruncated: Only the first {limit} characters of the page were summarised.
sumSendsTo: This text and the page's title go to {provider} ({model}) and nowhere else. Fields, hidden parts and anything you typed are left out.
sumConsent: The main text of this page and its title will be sent to {provider} ({model}) and nowhere else. Fields, hidden parts and anything you typed are left out. Its own terms apply to what it does with the text. You are asked this once.
sumAgainHint: Back to the choice of length. Nothing is sent until you press “Summarise”.
aiSummaryNote: “Summarise this page” is in the right-click menu of a page and in the Wordvault popup while a provider is set up. It reads the page's main text only when you ask, shows how much that is, and sends it after you agree. A long page goes in several parts (up to 120,000 characters).
ptNoText: Wordvault found no visible text to translate on this page.
ptRequests: Sent in {count} requests, one after the other
ptTruncated: The page is very long: only the first {limit} of its {total} characters will be translated. The rest stays as it is.
ptSendsTo: The visible text of this page and its title go to {provider} ({model}) and nowhere else. Fields, hidden parts, code and anything you typed are left out.
ptConsent: The visible text of this page and its title will be sent to {provider} ({model}) and nowhere else. Fields, hidden parts, code and anything you typed are left out. Its own terms apply to what it does with the text. You are asked this once.
ptCost: Every request counts against your quota or is billed by your provider. A whole page is far more text than a word or a summary.
ptPartDone: {done} of {total} requests are done; what they translated is on the page.
ptSkipped: {count, plural, one {# piece of text stayed as it was even after a second try} other {# pieces of text stayed as they were even after a second try}} (no usable answer came, or the page changed them meanwhile).
ptLeftOut: The end of the page was beyond the limit and is not translated.
ptNewText: New text has appeared on the page (about {count} characters). It is not sent unless you say so.
ptCloseHint: Closing this puts the original text back. The translation stays in this tab's memory: opening it again brings it back at once, without a request.
ptFromMemory: {count, plural, one {# piece of text came back at once from this tab's memory} other {# pieces of text came back at once from this tab's memory}}; nothing was sent again.
aiPageNote: “Translate this page with AI” (experimental) is in the same two places. It replaces the page's visible text chunk by chunk and can always be undone with “Show original”. It sends far more text than the other features: the card shows how much before you agree (up to 100,000 characters).
